rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David and Solomon exemplify just rulers: Solomon advised his father when he saw a better judgment, and David promptly accepted it; rulers are tested by this conduct.
rows.anchor: It is this character which defines a good ruler and whomsoever God makes a ruler, He does so to judge this conduct.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their just and selfless conduct is why God blessed both father and son with prophethood and political authority.
rows.anchor: because of this character trait of the father and son that God blessed both with prophethood and reins of political authority.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David's God-connection was joined to his rule: he praised God among the mountains at night, and the birds joined his chants.
rows.anchor: the sounds of his hymns and prayers that glorified and praised God and even the birds would join him in chorus.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah portrays David as a melodious singer with a moving voice; his prayers take hymn form, and even the Psalms' translated poetry retains power to move hearts.
rows.anchor: It is evident from the Torah that David (sws) was a very melodious singer and also had a very moving voice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains singing with David is factual, not poetic imagery; a tuneful chant can draw other beings into praise.
rows.anchor: These words should not be regarded as some poetic utterance; they are a fact.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creation glorifies God, though people may not hear it; singing praise intensifies this response, which fervent and ardent souls can hear.
rows.anchor: The Qur’ ān has specified that each and every object of this universe is extolling the Almighty but we are not able to understand it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording meaning with David, rather than for David, shows that the mountains and birds joined his chants.
rows.anchor: the Almighty had made the mountains and birds join David (sws) in his chants.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is placed beside the mountains because their glorification is unusual, while birds' glorification is familiar.
rows.anchor: this word is pre-placed is that the glorification chants of the birds are well known whereas that of mountains is a unique thing.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God can make such things happen and put creatures and inanimate things at someone's service; these favors are gifts, not human achievements.
rows.anchor: imply that only God can do these tasks none else.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David was a devoted servant of God and a valiant soldier; the verse refers to the body armour he invented, which was unmatched and prominent in classical war poetry.
rows.anchor: The verse refers to the body armour which David (sws) invented.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The armour was the key war attire of its time and made David's army formidable, though such equipment is obsolete now.
rows.anchor: In the war attire of those times, it was this armour which was the most important.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage contrasts David's moving devotional songs, which melt mountains, with military inventions and assaults that awed enemies.
rows.anchor: The purpose here is to show that he was both a God-devoted person and someone with great military might:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse challenges its audience to be grateful like David, whose austere character combined worldly power with devotion; God's grateful servants avoid slavery to worldly grandeur.
rows.anchor: It is this amalgation of worldly and next-worldly traits that God requires and such are His grateful people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām before Solomon signals an omitted verb; with this preposition the verb means to make something serve someone, so the winds were subdued for Solomon.
rows.anchor: When this verb occurs with the preposition ل,it means putting something into the service of someone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon's reign saw extraordinary naval growth: sails enabled voyages to India and western islands, and the fleet and its ports were prominent.
rows.anchor: David (sws) had a very large land force but it was in the reign of Solomon (sws) that the sea force made unparallelled advancements.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon's sails could navigate stormy winds and support long voyages in varying conditions; this technology explains the statement that God made strong winds serve him.
rows.anchor: Solomon (sws) had invented such sails which would allow ships to navigate smoothly in stormy winds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed land refers to Palestine, Syria, and surrounding territory, prized for fertility and trade.
rows.anchor: The words “a land in which We had placed blessings” refer to the land of Palestine and Syria etc.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording about God's knowledge also appears, with a slight change, in the account of Abraham at 21:51, which Islahi says he explained there.
rows.anchor: also occurred in verse 51 with a slight change in connection with Abraham (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew Solomon's capacities and granted him control of the winds, while continuing to observe how he used that power.
rows.anchor: After blessing him with this power, God did not become aloof; He continued to observe how Solomon (sws) used it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Modern scientists wrongly credit cosmological achievements to themselves; their success depends on intellect and guidance bestowed by God.
rows.anchor: Instead of regarding their cosmological achievements to be a blessing of God, they think that these are the result of their own competence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Claiming power as one's own encourages the further error that natural forces may be used without restraint or accountability.
rows.anchor: Once a person wrongly thinks that all his inventions owe themselves to his ability, another wrong notion springs forth which is even more destructive:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Providence remains aware of everything and will hold people accountable for abusing the natural powers entrusted to them.
rows.anchor: it is aware of everything and when this is so

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David and Solomon recognized their success as God's gifts and acted knowing they would answer to Him; that awareness produces gratitude and obedience, a theme to be developed in al-Naml.
rows.anchor: Both David (sws) and Solomon (sws) knew this fact very well. For this reason, even after achieving great success at both land and sea, they were never misled to think that all this was due to their own abilities;

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devils made subservient to Solomon are rebellious jinn.
rows.anchor: The devils referred to are the ones that were subservient to Solomon (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an and Torah describe Solomon's organized army as humans, jinn, and birds; Qur'an 27:17 is cited, along with an account of a jinn offering to bring the Queen of Sheba's throne.
rows.anchor: It is evident from both the Qur’ ān and the Torah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A powerful jinn told Solomon it could bring the Queen of Sheba's throne before his court was dismissed.
rows.anchor: before his court was dismissed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon's jinn dived for corals and pearls and performed other errands; bringing such harmful elements into human service was a notable achievement.
rows.anchor: These jinn would dive into the oceans to

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A capable ruler should employ both beneficial and otherwise harmful elements for society's development and progress.
rows.anchor: The real task before a competent ruler is not only to employ the beneficial elements but also those otherwise for the development and progress of society.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi points to his earlier discussion of Solomon's ability to subdue devils under 2:102, in the account of Harut and Marut.
rows.anchor: We have already discussed in detail the knowledge that was given to Solomon (sws) to subdue devils under verse 102 of Sūrah al-Baqarah where the incident of Hārūt and Mārūt is mentioned.

rows.speaker: Some people
rows.claim: Some identify the devils as disbelieving nations under Solomon's control.
rows.anchor: Some people are of the opinion that devils here refer to those disbelieving nations who were under his control.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects that reading as linguistically unjust: devils can secondarily denote rebellious elements among disbelieving peoples, but primarily denotes rebellious jinn, never whole disbelieving nations.
rows.anchor: It can refer to miscreant elements among disbelieving nations but that too in a secondary way – never primarily.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon could not control the devils independently; God kept them under watch so none escaped or rebelled, which would have caused havoc.
rows.anchor: God Who had given them in His control and He was watching over them so that none could escape

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who think they have mastered natural forces and cannot lose them are ignorant: control of steam, gas, electricity, and the atom is possible only by God's leave.
rows.anchor: If today man has got control over steam, gas, electricity and the atom etc, it is only because God has made this possible for him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human control lasts only as long as God wills; if He loosens His hold, the forces behind great achievements can wreak havoc.
rows.anchor: If God loosens His grip over them, these forces through which such huge achievements have been made will wreak havoc.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After David and Solomon as exemplary grateful servants, Islahi turns to prophets who exemplify patience, beginning with Job.
rows.anchor: After citing two outstanding exponents of gratitude

rows.speaker: Bible
rows.claim: The Bible describes Job as a righteous man in Uz, blessed with a large family, enormous herds and servants, and unmatched wealth in the East.
rows.anchor: It is evident from the Bible that he was a very righteous person who lived in Uz.

rows.speaker: Bible
rows.claim: The Biblical account gives Job seven sons, three daughters, extensive livestock, and many servants.
rows.anchor: He had seven sons and three daughters.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite his wealth, Job was deeply grateful and obedient to God and remained free of sin.
rows.anchor: However, in spite of this splendour he was very grateful and obedient to God.

rows.speaker: Satan and his agents
rows.claim: Satan and his agents alleged (Job 4:9-11) that Job's righteousness depended on his prosperity and that he would cease to be grateful if deprived of it.
rows.anchor: This righteousness of his was looked upon with jealousy by Satan and his agents.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Biblical story (Job 1:20-22) says Job lost his herds, servants, children, wealth, and splendour, yet worshipped and praised God, accepting that God gives and takes away.
rows.anchor: The Lord gave and the Lord has taken away; may the name of the Lord be praised.

rows.speaker: Bible
rows.claim: The Bible (Job 2:7-8) says Job developed painful sores from head to foot and scraped himself with pottery while sitting among ashes.
rows.anchor: Afflicted Job with painful sores from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head.

rows.speaker: Bible
rows.claim: Job endured illness patiently and trusted God; after praying for his friends, his fortunes were restored twofold, his family gathered around him, and he lived to see four generations (Job 42:10-16).
rows.anchor: After Job had prayed for his friends

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Job's supplication eloquently names his suffering but leaves the request unstated, entrusting the matter to God's mercy.
rows.anchor: Though Job (sws) referred to his pain and suffering, he did not utter the purpose of the supplication and left it to God’s mercy.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Job presents his grief and trusts that whatever God does will accord with divine mercy and bring him blessing.
rows.anchor: whatever God will do will be befitting to His mercy and this will have blessings for Job (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Complete contentment with God's decisions is linked with the Hereafter's status called raḍiyatan marḍiyyah.
rows.anchor: It is this state which is called complete contentment on the decisions of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly trials make it very difficult to know whether a person's desired outcome would truly be good for them.
rows.anchor: very difficult to determine from the trials and circumstances a person passes through in this world if their good outcome is good for a person
